# Introduction

Bengaluru is the only Indian city where the OAQ platform has two independent
PM2.5 monitor networks at the same time. The first network is CPCB, the
government reference network of regulatory-grade Continuous Ambient Air Quality
Monitoring Stations. The second network is Airnet, a dense network of low-cost
sensors that CSTEP operates.

This article compares the two networks in the same city for the same months
(March to April 2026). The question is whether the low-cost Airnet sensors give
the same signal as the CPCB reference network. A sensor network can show the
correct daily trend but report an incorrect level. Thus, we examine the trend,
the level, and the spatial coverage separately.

If the dense low-cost sensors give accurate data, they can supply data for the
areas that the sparse official network does not monitor.

---

# Data sources

The same functions read the two networks from the OAQ platform. Only the
`provider` argument is different. For each station, the functions return daily
means.

| Network | `provider` | Role | Pollutants | Density |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPCB | `"cpcb"` | Regulatory reference | PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NOx, met | Sparse |
| Airnet (CSTEP) | `"airnet"` | Low-cost sensors | PM2.5, PM10 | Dense |

---

# Setup

```{r packages}
library(vayuayan)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
```

```{r paths}
vignettes_dir <- here::here("vignettes")
fig_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "figures/blr_networks")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

---

# Fetch both networks

```{r oaq-session}
session <- oaq_session()
```

`oaq_fetch_monthly_stations()` gets the data for all stations of each provider
in a city for the selected months. It returns one tidy table of daily readings,
with the station coordinates.

```{r fetch-data, cache=TRUE}
both <- oaq_fetch_monthly_stations(
  session, c("cpcb", "airnet"),
  year = 2026, months = c("03", "04"), city = "Bengaluru"
) |>
  mutate(network = recode(provider,
    cpcb   = "CPCB reference",
    airnet = "Airnet low-cost"
  ))

both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25)) |>
  group_by(network) |>
  summarise(
    stations     = n_distinct(station_id),
    station_days = n(),
    median_pm25  = round(median(pm25), 1),
    iqr_low      = round(quantile(pm25, 0.25), 1),
    iqr_high     = round(quantile(pm25, 0.75), 1),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bengaluru PM2.5 coverage, March to April 2026")
```

The figures use these colors for the networks:

```{r colours}
net_colors <- c(
  "CPCB reference"  = "#d73027",
  "Airnet low-cost" = "#4575b4"
)
```

---

# Daily city trend

For each network and day, we calculate the median of all stations (the city
signal). We also calculate the inter-quartile range (the spread between sensors).
If the low-cost network gives the same signal as the reference network, the two
median lines will move together.

```{r daily-summary}
daily <- both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25)) |>
  group_by(network, date) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(pm25),
    p25 = quantile(pm25, 0.25),
    p75 = quantile(pm25, 0.75),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r daily-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Daily city-median PM2.5 in Bengaluru, March to April 2026. Lines show the cross-station median for each network. Ribbons show the inter-quartile range. The two networks have the same day-to-day trend. Airnet (blue) stays below the CPCB reference (red) for the full period. The difference is largest on days with high pollution."}
ggplot(daily, aes(x = date, colour = network, fill = network)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), alpha = 0.18, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", colour = "orange", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text",
    x = min(daily$date), y = 17,
    label = "WHO 24hr (15 µg/m³)", size = 3, colour = "tan4", hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d %b", date_breaks = "1 week") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "Bengaluru daily PM2.5: CPCB reference vs Airnet low-cost (2026)",
    subtitle = "Line = cross-station median | ribbon = inter-quartile range",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    caption  = "Source: OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in), providers cpcb + airnet"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig1_daily_trend.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Day-matched agreement

For each day, we plot the Airnet city median against the CPCB city median.
Points on the 1:1 line show that the low-cost network gives the same value as
the reference network. A fit line below the 1:1 line shows that Airnet reads
low. A slope less than 1 shows that the Airnet response is too small when
pollution increases.

```{r day-matched}
matched <- daily |>
  select(network, date, median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = network, values_from = median) |>
  rename(cpcb = `CPCB reference`, airnet = `Airnet low-cost`) |>
  filter(!is.na(cpcb), !is.na(airnet))

fit <- lm(airnet ~ cpcb, data = matched)
r_val <- cor(matched$cpcb, matched$airnet)
bias <- mean(matched$airnet - matched$cpcb)

cat("Matched days:", nrow(matched), "\n")
cat("Pearson r:", round(r_val, 3), "\n")
cat("Mean bias (Airnet − CPCB):", round(bias, 1), "µg/m³\n")
cat("Slope:", round(coef(fit)[2], 2), "\n")
```

```{r day-matched-plot, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Airnet vs CPCB city-median PM2.5, day-matched (March to April 2026). Each point is one day. The dashed line is 1:1. The red line is the linear fit."}
ggplot(matched, aes(x = cpcb, y = airnet)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(colour = "#4575b4", size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate("text",
    x = min(matched$cpcb), y = max(matched$airnet),
    label = sprintf(
      "r = %.2f\nbias = %+.1f µg/m³\nslope = %.2f",
      r_val, bias, coef(fit)[2]
    ),
    hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4, colour = "grey20"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  labs(
    title = "Day-matched agreement: Airnet vs CPCB",
    x = expression(paste("CPCB city median PM"[2.5])),
    y = expression(paste("Airnet city median PM"[2.5])),
    caption = "Source: OAQ platform | Bengaluru | March to April 2026"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig2_day_matched.png"), width = 6, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Spatial coverage

The largest difference between the two networks is density. The map shows all
stations on the ward boundaries of Bengaluru. The size of each point shows the
mean PM2.5 of the station for the period.

```{r blr-boundary}
blr_boundary <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/bengaluru.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) |> sf::st_transform(4326)
```

```{r station-means}
station_means <- both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25), !is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) |>
  group_by(network, station_id, lat, lon) |>
  summarise(mean_pm25 = mean(pm25), n_days = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_days >= 10)

station_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(station_means, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
```

```{r station-map, fig.height=7, fig.width=9, fig.cap="Density of the monitor networks in Bengaluru. Red points are CPCB reference stations. Blue points are Airnet low-cost sensors. Point size shows mean PM2.5 (March to April 2026). The low-cost network is approximately 4x denser."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = blr_boundary, fill = "grey97", colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(
    data = station_sf,
    aes(colour = network, size = mean_pm25),
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), name = expression(paste("Mean PM"[2.5]))) +
  labs(
    title = "Bengaluru monitoring networks: reference vs low-cost",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "CPCB: %d stations | Airnet: %d stations (≥10 valid days)",
      sum(station_means$network == "CPCB reference"),
      sum(station_means$network == "Airnet low-cost")
    ),
    caption = "Source: OAQ platform + BharatViz ward boundaries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    axis.text       = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig3_network_map.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Control for location

The city-median comparison has a confound. The two networks do not cover the
same areas. Most CPCB stations are in central Bengaluru, but Airnet also has
sensors at the periphery. If the air at the periphery is cleaner, Airnet will
read lower, even with a perfect sensor. In that case, the bias above is an
effect of the station locations, not of the sensors.

To separate the two effects, we pair each Airnet sensor with its nearest CPCB
station. We keep only the pairs that are a short distance apart, so that the two
stations in each pair have almost the same location. If the low bias stays after
this control, the cause is the sensors, not the geography.

```{r distance-control}
cpcb_st <- station_means |> filter(network == "CPCB reference")
air_st <- station_means |> filter(network == "Airnet low-cost")

paired <- nearest_stations(
  air_st, cpcb_st,
  k = 1, from_id = "station_id", to_id = "station_id"
) |>
  left_join(
    air_st |> select(station_id, airnet_pm25 = mean_pm25),
    by = c("from_id" = "station_id")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cpcb_st |> select(station_id, cpcb_pm25 = mean_pm25),
    by = c("to_id" = "station_id")
  )

control_table <- paired |>
  crossing(radius = c(3, 5, 8)) |>
  filter(dist_km <= radius) |>
  group_by(radius) |>
  summarise(
    `Co-located pairs` = n(),
    `Mean Airnet`      = round(mean(airnet_pm25), 1),
    `Mean CPCB`        = round(mean(cpcb_pm25), 1),
    `Mean difference`  = round(mean(airnet_pm25 - cpcb_pm25), 1)
  ) |>
  mutate(`Max pairing distance` = paste0("≤ ", radius, " km"), .before = 1) |>
  select(-radius)

uncontrolled_diff <- round(median(air_st$mean_pm25) - median(cpcb_st$mean_pm25), 1)

knitr::kable(control_table,
  caption = sprintf(
    "Airnet minus CPCB after distance pairing. Uncontrolled city-median difference: %s µg/m³.",
    uncontrolled_diff
  )
)
```

The median distance from an Airnet sensor to a CPCB station is approximately
3 km, so the pairs are close. In the table above, the low bias changes very
little when we keep only the co-located pairs. Thus, the bias is a property of
the sensors, not of their locations.

---

# Distribution comparison

The daily median does not show the shape of the readings. A plot of the full
distribution of station-days for each network shows where the networks overlap
and where they are different. A narrower low-cost distribution can show lower
real variability, or sensors that smooth the data.

```{r distribution-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Distribution of daily station PM2.5 readings by network, March to April 2026. Each observation is one station on one day."}
obs <- both |> filter(!is.na(pm25))

ggplot(obs, aes(x = pm25, fill = network, colour = network)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(
    data = obs |> group_by(network) |> summarise(m = median(pm25), .groups = "drop"),
    aes(xintercept = m, colour = network), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³"), limits = c(0, 150)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "PM2.5 reading distribution: CPCB vs Airnet",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines = network medians",
    x        = expression(paste("Daily station PM"[2.5])),
    y        = "Density",
    caption  = "Source: OAQ platform | Bengaluru | March to April 2026"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig4_distribution.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Conclusion

```{r conclusion-stats, echo=FALSE}
cpcb_med <- round(median(both$pm25[both$provider == "cpcb"], na.rm = TRUE), 1)
airnet_med <- round(median(both$pm25[both$provider == "airnet"], na.rm = TRUE), 1)
r_round <- round(r_val, 2)
bias_round <- round(bias, 1)
slope_round <- round(coef(fit)[2], 2)
n_cpcb <- sum(station_means$network == "CPCB reference")
n_airnet <- sum(station_means$network == "Airnet low-cost")
```

In Bengaluru, for March to April 2026, the day-to-day pattern of the Airnet
low-cost network is correct, but its magnitude is incorrect.

The day-to-day patterns of the two networks agree well. The two city-median lines increase
and decrease on the same days. The day-matched correlation is `r r_round`.
Thus, a low-cost network can show reliably when the air in Bengaluru becomes
worse.

The Airnet magnitude is too low. The network-median PM2.5 of Airnet is
`r airnet_med` µg/m³, and the value for CPCB is `r cpcb_med` µg/m³. The mean
bias is `r bias_round` µg/m³. The regression slope of `r slope_round` shows that
the difference increases when concentrations increase. The two networks agree on
clean days. On the pollution peaks that CPCB records, the Airnet values are
lower by larger amounts.

The cause is the sensors, not the geography. When we pair each Airnet sensor
with a CPCB station a few kilometers away, the low bias stays almost the same.
Range compression of this type is a known property of low-cost sensors. It is
the primary reason not to use raw Airnet values as absolute levels.

The advantage of the low-cost network is coverage. Airnet has `r n_airnet`
usable stations, and CPCB has `r n_cpcb`. The Airnet stations are also at the
periphery of the city, where the reference network has no monitors.

Thus, the two networks supply different information, and one network cannot
replace the other. Airnet is reliable for trends and for data in areas without
reference stations. Before you use Airnet readings as absolute concentrations,
you must calibrate them against the CPCB reference. This calibration is most
necessary during periods of high pollution. Also, only the reference network
measures NO2, SO2, CO, and O3. Airnet does not measure these pollutants.
